mgmt_bio.text: Martin Pibworth became Chief Executive of SSE plc on 17 July 2025, having joined the company in 1998 as an energy trader and progressed through a series of commercial roles, becoming Managing Director, Energy Portfolio Management and a member of the then Management Board in 2012. In 2014 he was appointed Managing Director, Wholesale, taking responsibility for SSE's electricity generation portfolio and associated capital investment programme, overseeing the development of its flexible generation fleet and growing renewables. He joined the SSE Board in 2017, and as Chief Commercial Officer oversaw SSE's Renewables, Thermal, Energy Markets and Energy Customer Solutions businesses. He was appointed following a competitive recruitment process, succeeding Alistair Phillips-Davies after the 2025 annual general meeting.

sentences.quote: Martin joined SSE in 1998 and has progressively held a number of key commercial roles in the Company over the last three decades, joining the Executive Committee in 2012 and the Board in 2017.
sentences.text: Pibworth joined SSE in 1998, ran its wholesale and commercial activities and sat on the board from 2017, becoming chief executive in July 2025 after a competitive succession process led by the chair and nomination committee with external recruitment support.

In the year to March 2026 the group reported EPS of 153.5p towards the top end of guidance, record capital expenditure of GBP 3.6bn and a recommended 7% dividend increase, with FY27 and FY30 earnings targets unchanged.

Capital allocation has tilted to regulated networks, which take about 80% of the reiterated GBP 33bn five-year plan, part-funded by a November 2025 equity issuance that contributed to a 5% fall in adjusted EPS.

thesis_pillars.text: SSE plc, the UK-listed energy group, is executing a fully funded GBP 33bn five-year investment plan to 2029/30, with around 80% or GBP 27bn going into regulated UK electricity Networks and around 20% or GBP 6bn into Renewables and system Flexibility. That spend is targeted to lift gross regulated asset value at roughly a 25% CAGR and drive a 7-9% adjusted EPS CAGR to 225-250 pence by 2029/30, with index-linked EBITDA making up about 80% of group earnings. Management reaffirms a progressive dividend policy targeting 5-10% annual growth from a 64.2 pence 2024/25 baseline. Funding comes from operating cashflow, additional debt and hybrid capital, a GBP 2bn equity placing and targeted asset rotation, while retaining strong investment-grade ratings.
